fatal_errors: Identifies DFT composition optimization as the fabrication method rather than liquid-metal dealloying by immersion in molten Cu.
Omits the directionally segregated WTaVTi precursor and preferential replacement of Ti/V-rich interdendritic channels.
Misses the reported 1200 °C, 96 h vacuum-sealed reaction conditions.
Does not reconstruct the bicontinuous aligned RHEA-ligament/Cu-channel architecture or the W-rich passivating interlayer.
The proposed 20% stability improvement, 15% falsification threshold, temperature range, and pressure range are unsupported inventions.
Treats a computational calculation as if it directly forms a large-scale composite, without specifying an actual synthesis route.
explanation: The hypothesis only broadly recognizes that RHEA–Cu thermodynamic incompatibility and interfacial stability matter. It does not identify the central method—liquid-metal dealloying of directionally segregated WTaVTi in molten Cu—or the selective Ti extraction/Cu replacement mechanism that enables millimeter-scale penetration and a stable aligned microstructure. It also omits the W-rich interfacial passivation layer and all relevant structural, thermal, and irradiation outcomes. The proposed comparison is weakly testable in principle, but 'with versus without DFT' is not a controlled materials intervention unless DFT-selected compositions and fabrication conditions are explicitly defined. No evidence supports the quantitative claims.
